description: Learning-path eval topics (test plan §6.3): each topic's core sections, listed by hand from its official docs (or, with none, the standard outline of the subject). Coverage = core sections matched by a path's included concepts ÷ core sections. DRAFT by the agent (2026-10-03), to be reviewed by the owner.

sections.name: Numbers, variables and arithmetic
sections.description: Using Python as a calculator: int and float, operators, assigning variables.

sections.name: Strings
sections.description: String literals, indexing and slicing, concatenation, common string operations.

sections.name: Lists
sections.description: Creating lists, indexing, slicing, appending and other list methods.

sections.name: Conditions and if statements
sections.description: Booleans, comparisons, if / elif / else.

sections.name: Loops
sections.description: for loops over sequences, range(), while loops, break and continue.

sections.name: Defining functions
sections.description: def, parameters and arguments, return values, default and keyword arguments.

sections.name: Tuples, sets and dictionaries
sections.description: The other built-in collections and when to use each.

sections.name: Modules and imports
sections.description: import, the standard library, writing and using your own modules and packages.

sections.name: Input, output and files
sections.description: Formatting output (f-strings), reading input, reading and writing files.

sections.name: Errors and exceptions
sections.description: Syntax errors vs exceptions, try / except / finally, raising exceptions.

sections.name: Classes and objects
sections.description: Defining classes, attributes and methods, creating instances, inheritance.

sections.name: What version control and Git are
sections.description: Why version control; Git stores snapshots and is distributed.

sections.name: Installing and setting up Git
sections.description: Installing Git and first-time configuration (user name, email) with git config.

sections.name: Creating or cloning a repository
sections.description: git init and git clone.

sections.name: Working directory, staging area and commits
sections.description: The three states; git add to stage, git commit to record a snapshot.

sections.name: Checking status and changes
sections.description: git status and git diff to see what changed.

sections.name: Viewing commit history
sections.description: git log and its common options.

sections.name: Undoing changes
sections.description: Amending a commit, unstaging and discarding changes (restore / reset).

sections.name: Working with remotes
sections.description: Remotes, git fetch, git pull and git push.

sections.name: Branches
sections.description: What a branch is, creating and switching branches.

sections.name: Merging and merge conflicts
sections.description: Merging branches and resolving conflicts.

sections.name: Rebasing
sections.description: What rebase does, how it differs from merge, and when not to rebase.

topics.sectionsSource: The standard outline of the subject (as in encyclopedia articles such as Britannica's "French Revolution"); no official docs exist, so this is the topic-without-official-docs case.

sections.name: Causes of the Revolution
sections.description: The Ancien Régime, the three estates, the financial crisis, Enlightenment ideas.

sections.name: Estates-General and National Assembly
sections.description: The Estates-General of 1789, the Third Estate's National Assembly, the Tennis Court Oath.

sections.name: Storming of the Bastille
sections.description: 14 July 1789 and the popular uprising in Paris.

sections.name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
sections.description: The August 1789 declaration and the abolition of feudal privileges.

sections.name: Constitutional monarchy
sections.description: The Constitution of 1791, the flight to Varennes, the Legislative Assembly.

sections.name: War with European powers
sections.description: War with Austria and Prussia from 1792 and its effect on the Revolution.

sections.name: Fall of the monarchy and the First Republic
sections.description: August 1792 uprising, the National Convention, the Republic declared.

sections.name: Execution of Louis XVI
sections.description: The king's trial and execution in January 1793.

sections.name: The Reign of Terror
sections.description: Robespierre, the Committee of Public Safety, mass executions (1793–94).

sections.name: Thermidor and the Directory
sections.description: Robespierre's fall in 1794 and the Directory government (1795–99).

sections.name: Napoleon's rise and the end of the Revolution
sections.description: The coup of 18 Brumaire (1799) and the Consulate.

sections.name: Legacy of the Revolution
sections.description: Its lasting effects on France, Europe and ideas of rights and democracy.
